newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Ent's HK IPO 1,250-1,300 times subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Ent's HK IPO 1,250-1,300 times subscribed.

text.p: Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's Hong Kong initial public offering (IPO) was 1,250 to 1,300 times subscribed, a source close to the underwriters told Reuters on Monday.
The subscription level makes the red chip's IPO the most popular ever in Hong Kong, smashing the previous subscription record held by GITIC Enterprises Ltd, also a red chip.
GITIC's initial public offering in March was 892 times subscribed.
The source said the number of void applications was higher than other IPOs. "The spoilage rate was slightly higher. There were lots of first time applicants."

Beijing Enterprises, a conglomerate controlled by the Beijing municipal government, offered 150 million shares at HK$12.48 in a global IPO. Ten percent was offered in Hong Kong and 90 percent to international investors.
The grey market price for the stock was quoted at HK$41-HK$43 on Monday.
The official subscription level is due to be released on Wednesday and the stock is due to begin trading on Thursday.
